certGates.readinessRule: Score >=80% twice on separate sittings before booking the real exam.

questions.q: A user's laptop screen flickers only when the lid is moved. Which component is the most likely cause?
choices: Failing inverter cable / display ribbon cable through the hinge
questions.explain: Flicker tied to lid movement points to the display cable flexing at the hinge; drivers and RAM would fail regardless of lid position.

questions.q: A tablet will not connect to the corporate Wi-Fi but connects fine to a phone hotspot. What should you check first?
choices: Whether the tablet supports the corporate network's Wi-Fi security/802.1X requirements
Whether the tablet case is metal
questions.explain: Hotspot success proves the radio works; failure on one specific network points to that network's security or configuration requirements.

questions.q: Which laptop feature lets a technician replace the battery, RAM, and drive without special tools?
choices: Field-replaceable units designed for user/technician service
questions.explain: Serviceable designs expose FRUs; soldered or sealed designs prevent field replacement.

questions.q: A phone overheats and drains quickly after a third-party repair. Which is the most likely cause?
choices: A pinched or damaged battery/thermal assembly from the repair
questions.explain: Sudden thermal/battery behavior right after a repair implicates the repair work itself — typically battery or thermal-pad damage.

questions.q: Which port and protocol does HTTPS use by default?
questions.explain: HTTPS runs over TCP port 443; 80 is HTTP, 53 is DNS, 25 is SMTP.

questions.q: A PC gets a 169.254.x.x address. What does this indicate?
choices: The DHCP server could not be reached, so APIPA assigned a link-local address
questions.explain: 169.254.0.0/16 is APIPA: Windows self-assigns it when no DHCP response arrives.

questions.q: Which cable type is correct for a 40-meter run to a gigabit switch in an office with fluorescent lighting and EMI?
choices: Multimode fiber is the only option
questions.explain: Shielded Cat6A resists EMI and supports 10GbE at distance; fiber works but is overkill for a 40 m office run.

questions.q: A user can ping 8.8.8.8 but cannot browse any website by name. What is the most likely fault?
questions.explain: Pinging an IP proves L3 connectivity; name resolution failing while IPs work isolates the fault to DNS.

questions.q: Which wireless standard operates exclusively in the 6 GHz band?
questions.explain: Wi-Fi 6E (802.11ax extension) added 6 GHz operation; 802.11n is 2.4/5 GHz, ac is 5 GHz.

questions.q: A PC randomly reboots under load but is stable at idle. Temperatures are normal. What should you suspect first?
questions.explain: Reboots under load with normal thermals are the classic signature of a PSU that cannot sustain peak draw.

questions.q: Which RAM type is correct for a modern desktop motherboard with DDR5 slots?
questions.explain: DDR generations are physically keyed differently; a DDR5 board requires DDR5 modules.

questions.q: An NVMe SSD is not detected in BIOS. The slot is M.2. What is the most likely cause?
choices: The M.2 slot is SATA-only and does not support NVMe
The SSD needs a driver installed in BIOS
NVMe drives require a RAID card
questions.explain: Some M.2 slots are keyed/routed for SATA only; an NVMe drive in a SATA-only slot will not appear.

questions.q: Which symptom best indicates a failing hard drive rather than a software issue?
choices: Slow boot times after an update
Repeated clicking sounds and SMART errors
High CPU usage in Task Manager
questions.explain: Clicking (head actuator faults) plus SMART errors are hardware-level failure indicators.

questions.q: A custom build needs to drive 4K video editing. Which component choice matters most?
choices: A discrete GPU with adequate VRAM plus a CPU with enough cores
questions.explain: 4K editing is GPU- and CPU-bound; VRAM and core count determine timeline performance.

questions.q: What is the purpose of a motherboard's CMOS battery?
choices: To power the CPU during sleep
To retain BIOS/UEFI settings and the real-time clock when unplugged
To back up the hard drive
questions.explain: The coin-cell battery preserves firmware settings and RTC time with no mains power.

questions.q: What is the primary difference between Type 1 and Type 2 hypervisors?
choices: Type 1 runs directly on hardware; Type 2 runs on top of a host OS
Type 1 is free; Type 2 is paid
questions.explain: Type 1 (bare-metal, e.g., Hyper-V Server/ESXi) sits on hardware; Type 2 (e.g., VirtualBox) is an application on a host OS.

questions.q: A company wants to move CapEx to OpEx and scale resources on demand. Which cloud model fits?
questions.explain: Public cloud converts capital expense to operational expense with elastic scaling.

questions.q: Which is a key resource requirement to verify before deploying VMs on a host?
choices: Available CPU, RAM, storage IOPS, and network bandwidth versus VM demand
questions.explain: VM density planning requires matching aggregate VM demand against host compute, memory, storage, and network capacity.

questions.q: What is the correct FIRST step in the standard troubleshooting methodology?
choices: Identify the problem: gather information and question users
questions.explain: Methodology starts with identifying the problem before theorizing or acting.

questions.q: After implementing a fix, what is the required next step?
choices: Verify full system functionality and implement preventive measures
questions.explain: Verification plus preventive measures (and documentation) complete the methodology.

questions.q: A printer prints blank pages. Ink/toner is full. What is the most likely cause?
choices: Protective tape/seal left on the cartridge or a clogged printhead
questions.explain: Full consumables plus blank output points to the transfer path: unremoved seals or clogged heads.

questions.q: Intermittent network drops affect one workstation. Swapping the patch cable fixes it permanently. What was the fault?
choices: A damaged or marginal patch cable
questions.explain: Single-host intermittent issues resolved by cable swap implicate the cable itself.

questions.q: A PC shows no display but fans spin and drives sound active. What should you check first?
choices: Monitor cable, input source, and reseat RAM/GPU
questions.explain: No-display-with-power is most often cable/input or a POST-stopping reseat issue; check the simple external causes first.

questions.q: Which tool verifies that a cable run is wired to the correct pinout standard?
questions.explain: A cable tester checks continuity and correct pin-to-pin mapping.

questions.q: A laptop battery swells and the trackpad lifts. What is the correct action?
choices: Puncture the battery to release pressure
Power down, do not charge or puncture, and replace the battery following safety procedures
Keep using it until it dies
questions.explain: Swollen lithium batteries are a fire hazard: stop use, never puncture, replace per safety procedure.

questions.q: Which Windows tool shows startup programs, services, and boot configuration?
questions.explain: msconfig manages boot options, services, and startup items.

questions.q: A user needs to join a Windows Pro machine to a domain. Where is this done?
choices: System Properties > Computer Name > Change > Domain
questions.explain: Domain membership is set in System Properties under Computer Name/Domain Changes.

questions.q: Which command-line tool displays the IP configuration of a Windows host?
questions.explain: ipconfig shows addresses, mask, gateway, and DNS for each adapter.

questions.q: What does the `chkdsk /r` command do?
choices: Locates bad sectors and recovers readable information while checking disk integrity
questions.explain: /r implies /f plus a full surface scan for bad sectors with data recovery.

questions.q: Which Windows feature allows rolling back a faulty driver update?
questions.explain: Device Manager's Roll Back Driver reverts to the previously installed driver.

questions.q: A workstation cannot reach a file share by name but can by IP. Which OS-level setting should you verify?
choices: The DNS server addresses on the adapter
questions.explain: Name resolution for shares depends on DNS (or NetBIOS); IP access working isolates it to name resolution.

questions.q: Which partition style is required to boot Windows from a disk larger than 2 TB?
questions.explain: GPT supports disks over 2 TB and UEFI boot; MBR is limited to 2 TB.

questions.q: What is the purpose of Windows Safe Mode?
choices: Booting with minimal drivers/services to diagnose problems
questions.explain: Safe Mode loads a minimal driver set so faulty drivers or software can be isolated.

questions.q: Which is the strongest password policy control against brute-force attacks?
choices: Account lockout after failed attempts plus complexity and length requirements
questions.explain: Lockout throttles guessing; complexity and length raise the search space.

questions.q: A user receives an email asking for credentials with a link to a lookalike domain. This is:
questions.explain: Credential harvesting via deceptive email and lookalike domains is phishing.

questions.q: Which Windows feature encrypts an entire drive to protect data if a laptop is stolen?
questions.explain: BitLocker provides full-disk encryption tied to TPM/PIN.

questions.q: What is the principle of least privilege?
choices: Grant users only the access required to do their jobs
questions.explain: Least privilege minimizes the blast radius of compromised accounts.

questions.q: Which is the best practice when disposing of a hard drive containing sensitive data?
choices: Degauss/destroy or cryptographically wipe per policy
questions.explain: Sensitive media requires verifiable destruction or wiping, never casual disposal.

questions.q: What does MFA protect against that a strong password alone does not?
choices: Credential theft/replay, since the attacker also needs the second factor
questions.explain: A second factor means a stolen password alone is insufficient.

questions.q: What is the correct order for malware remediation?
choices: Investigate, quarantine, disable System Restore, remediate, schedule scans, enable Restore, educate user
questions.explain: The standard sequence isolates the threat, removes it safely, and prevents reinfection.

questions.q: An application crashes on launch after an update. What is the best FIRST step?
choices: Check the application and OS event logs for the error
questions.explain: Logs identify the faulting module before any destructive action.

questions.q: A PC is extremely slow. Task Manager shows 100% disk usage from one process. What next?
choices: Identify the process; check for runaway indexing, AV scan, or failing drive, then act
questions.explain: Diagnose the specific consumer first — cause determines the fix.

questions.q: Which symptom most suggests a corrupted OS rather than a bad application?
choices: Multiple unrelated system functions fail and SFC finds integrity violations
questions.explain: System-wide failures plus SFC integrity violations point at OS corruption.

questions.q: What does Windows System Restore do?
choices: Reverts system files, drivers, and registry to a restore point without touching personal files
questions.explain: System Restore rolls back system state; personal files are preserved.

questions.q: A mobile app drains battery rapidly in the background. What is the best first step?
choices: Check battery usage stats, restrict background activity for the offending app
questions.explain: Battery stats identify the consumer; restricting its background activity is the targeted fix.

questions.q: Before opening a plugged-in desktop case, what must you do first?
choices: Power off, unplug, and use ESD protection
questions.explain: Unplug plus ESD strap prevents shock and electrostatic damage.

questions.q: A toner spill occurs. What is the correct cleanup?
choices: Use a toner-rated (HEPA/ESD-safe) vacuum; never a standard vacuum
Blow it with compressed air toward your face
questions.explain: Standard vacuums can ignite fine toner or blow it through; toner vacuums are filtered and ESD-safe.

questions.q: Which document records what changed, when, and why for IT systems?
questions.explain: Change records provide auditability and rollback reference.

questions.q: A user is upset about downtime. What is the professional response?
choices: Argue about whose fault it is
Acknowledge the impact, communicate status and ETA, and follow up
questions.explain: Professionalism: empathy, clear status, committed follow-up.

questions.q: Why should you document lessons learned after resolving a major incident?
choices: So the next technician can resolve it faster and preventive measures can be implemented
questions.explain: Documentation converts one incident into institutional knowledge and prevention.

questions.q: How many usable host addresses are in a /26 subnet?
questions.explain: 2^6 = 64 addresses minus network and broadcast = 62 usable.

questions.q: Which OSI layer do routers primarily operate at?
questions.explain: Routers forward based on IP addresses — the Network layer (L3).

questions.q: What is the purpose of a VLAN?
choices: Logically segment a switched network into separate broadcast domains
questions.explain: VLANs create isolated broadcast domains on shared switch hardware.

questions.q: Which IPv6 address type replaces IPv4 broadcast?
questions.explain: IPv6 has no broadcast; multicast serves one-to-many delivery.

questions.q: What does NAT primarily accomplish?
choices: Translate between private and public IP address spaces
questions.explain: NAT maps private RFC 1918 addresses to public addresses at the network edge.

questions.q: Which routing protocol is a link-state interior protocol?
questions.explain: OSPF is the classic link-state IGP; RIP is distance-vector, BGP is path-vector exterior.

questions.q: In the TCP three-way handshake, what is the correct sequence?
questions.explain: SYN → SYN-ACK → ACK establishes the connection.

questions.q: What is the default subnet mask for a Class C network in dotted decimal?
questions.explain: Class C default is /24 = 255.255.255.0.

questions.q: Which device separates collision domains but not broadcast domains?
questions.explain: Each switch port is its own collision domain; broadcasts still propagate without VLANs/routing.

questions.q: What is the main advantage of a full-mesh topology?
choices: Maximum redundancy — any single link failure leaves alternate paths
questions.explain: Full mesh connects every node to every other, surviving any single link failure.

questions.q: What is the maximum effective run length for Cat6 Ethernet?
questions.explain: 100 m total channel length (90 m solid + 10 m patch) is the standard limit.

questions.q: Which fiber connector uses a push-pull latch and is common in data centers?
questions.explain: LC's small form factor and latch dominate dense data-center patching.

questions.q: What does PoE allow?
choices: Power delivery over Ethernet cabling to devices like APs and cameras
questions.explain: Power over Ethernet carries DC power alongside data on twisted pair.

questions.q: Which 802.11 standard first introduced MU-MIMO?
questions.explain: 802.11ac added downlink MU-MIMO; ax extended it to uplink.

questions.q: In a SOHO router, what does enabling DHCP reservation accomplish?
choices: Assigns the same IP to a device by MAC address every time
questions.explain: Reservations bind a MAC to a fixed leased address.

questions.q: Which WAN technology uses labels to forward packets quickly across provider networks?
questions.explain: MPLS forwards on short labels rather than full IP lookups.

questions.q: What is the primary benefit of SD-WAN for branch offices?
choices: Centralized, policy-based control over multiple WAN links with failover
questions.explain: SD-WAN abstracts transport links under central policy with dynamic path selection.

questions.q: Which device regenerates and retimes a signal but does not filter traffic?
questions.explain: Repeaters amplify the signal at L1 with no forwarding decisions.

questions.q: What should you verify first when planning AP placement in an office?
choices: Coverage, capacity, channel plan, and interference sources via survey
questions.explain: A wireless survey determines AP count, placement, channels, and power.

questions.q: Which metric measures the time for a packet to travel to a destination and back?
questions.explain: Round-trip time quantifies latency for the path.

questions.q: What is the primary purpose of a network baseline?
choices: Establish normal performance values so anomalies can be detected
questions.explain: Baselines define 'normal' for comparison during incidents.

questions.q: Which tool captures and analyzes individual packets?
questions.explain: Protocol analyzers decode frames/packets for deep inspection.

questions.q: What does SNMP primarily provide?
choices: Monitoring and management of network devices via queries and traps
questions.explain: SNMP polls device OIDs and receives trap alerts for monitoring.

questions.q: In BC/DR planning, what does RTO define?
choices: How much data loss is acceptable
The maximum acceptable downtime before service restoration
questions.explain: Recovery Time Objective = how fast; RPO = how much data loss is tolerable.

questions.q: Which remote-access method gives a remote worker full network-layer access as if on-site?
questions.explain: A VPN extends the network to the remote endpoint at L3.

questions.q: Why maintain network documentation and diagrams?
choices: Faster troubleshooting, onboarding, and change planning
questions.explain: Current diagrams and configs cut mean-time-to-repair dramatically.

questions.q: Which is a common cause of intermittent connectivity that a baseline helps identify?
choices: Gradual bandwidth saturation or degrading hardware showing in trends
questions.explain: Trend data reveals saturation and degradation before they become outages.

questions.q: What is the function of syslog in network operations?
choices: Centralized collection of device log messages for review and alerting
questions.explain: Syslog aggregates device logs to one collector for analysis.

questions.q: Which attack floods a target with traffic to exhaust resources?
questions.explain: Distributed denial-of-service overwhelms capacity with volume.

questions.q: What does 802.1X provide on a wired/wireless network?
choices: Port-based network access control with authentication
questions.explain: 802.1X authenticates devices/users before granting network access.

questions.q: Which VPN type is best for always-on site-to-site connectivity between offices?
questions.explain: Site-to-site IPsec tunnels connect whole networks persistently.

questions.q: What is the security benefit of network segmentation?
choices: Limits lateral movement by containing breaches to segments
questions.explain: Segmentation confines compromise and enforces policy between zones.

questions.q: Which wireless security standard should be deployed today?
questions.explain: WPA2-Enterprise/WPA3 provide strong encryption and authentication; WEP/WPA are broken.

questions.q: What does a honeypot accomplish?
choices: Attract and detect attacker activity away from production
questions.explain: Decoy systems reveal attacker techniques and provide early warning.

questions.q: Users report slow access to a server. Ping shows high latency but no loss. What is indicated?
choices: Congestion or a degraded path, not a hard failure
questions.explain: High latency without loss suggests congestion/buffering rather than breakage.

questions.q: Which command traces the path packets take to a destination?
questions.explain: Traceroute maps each hop via TTL-expired ICMP messages.

questions.q: A new VLAN has no connectivity. Devices have correct IPs. What is the most likely miss?
choices: Bad patch cable on every device
The VLAN is not trunked/allowed on the uplink or lacks a gateway/SVI
questions.explain: Correct IPs with zero connectivity across a new VLAN usually means trunking or L3 interface misconfiguration.

questions.q: Duplicate IP addresses on a network cause what symptom?
choices: Intermittent connectivity and address conflicts for the affected hosts
questions.explain: Two hosts claiming one IP produces flapping, conflicts, and intermittent access.

questions.q: What is the first step when troubleshooting per the standard methodology?
questions.explain: Identification precedes theory, testing, and action.

questions.q: A fiber link shows high error counters. What should you check first?
choices: Dirty or damaged fiber connectors and bend radius
questions.explain: Physical-layer issues (contamination, bends, bad SFP) cause error counters on fiber.

questions.q: Which tool tests whether a specific TCP port is reachable on a remote host?
choices: Port scanner / telnet to the port / Test-NetConnection
questions.explain: Ping only tests ICMP; port reachability needs a TCP connection attempt.

questions.q: Wireless clients near one AP keep disconnecting while others are fine. Likely cause?
choices: Channel interference or a failing AP
questions.explain: Localized to one AP's coverage area implicates that AP or its RF environment.

questions.q: After a change, nothing works. What is the best immediate action?
choices: Reverse the change / roll back to the last known-good state
questions.explain: Change-management discipline: back out the change, then diagnose.

questions.q: What does an ARP table map?
questions.explain: ARP resolves L3 IPs to L2 MACs on the local segment.

questions.q: A speed/duplex mismatch between a PC and switch causes what?
choices: Late collisions, errors, and degraded throughput on the link
questions.explain: Mismatched duplex (often from hard-coded settings) produces collisions and errors.
